stories.headline: US-Iran Ceasefire Gets In-Principle Extension as US Blockade Fully Halts Iranian Maritime Trade

key_facts.fact: Mediators secured an 'in principle agreement' from the US and Iran to extend the ceasefire before it expires on April 22, to allow more diplomacy
key_facts.excerpt: regional officials said Wednesday they were making progress, telling The Associated Press that the United States and Iran had given an 'in principle agreement' to extend it to allow for more diplomacy

key_facts.fact: Three main sticking points derailed direct talks last weekend: Iran's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and compensation for wartime damages
key_facts.excerpt: mediators are pushing for a compromise on three main sticking points that derailed direct talks last weekend — Iran's nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz and compensation for wartime damages

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM declared the blockade of Iranian ports 'fully implemented'; no ships passed the blockade in the first 24 hours and six merchant vessels were turned around
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Central Command said Tuesday no ships made it past the blockade in the first 24 hours, while six merchant vessels complied with direction from U.S. forces to turn around

key_facts.fact: The US is seeking a 20-year halt to Iranian uranium enrichment; Iran has proposed five years. The US also demands dismantling of major enrichment facilities and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: uranium enrichment remains the main sticking point. The US is reportedly seeking a 20-year halt, while Iran has proposed five

key_facts.fact: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors held their first direct talks in decades in Washington; Lebanon called the meeting 'constructive' but Israel refused to commit to a ceasefire in southern Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter said the two countries are 'on the same side of the equation' in 'liberating Lebanon' from Hezbollah. Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad called the meeting 'constructive'

key_facts.fact: The war has killed at least 3,000 in Iran, more than 2,100 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, more than a dozen in Gulf states, and 13 US service members since it began February 28
key_facts.excerpt: The fighting has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, more than 2,100 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states. Thirteen U.S. service members have also been killed.

key_facts.fact: FT reports Iran's IRGC acquired a Chinese satellite in late 2024 to help target US military bases across the Middle East, citing leaked Iranian military documents
key_facts.excerpt: The Financial Times published an investigation on Wednesday claiming Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) acquired a Chinese satellite to help its forces target US military bases across the Middle East

stories.headline: IMF Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast to 3.1%, Warns Iran War Could Trigger Recession

key_facts.fact: IMF downgraded 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.3% in January; absent the war, it would have upgraded to 3.4% due to the tech investment boom and lower tariffs
key_facts.excerpt: The IMF downgraded its forecast for global growth to 3.1% in 2026 from the 3.3% it had forecast back in January... Absent the Middle East conflict, the IMF said it would have upgraded its growth outlook by 0.1 percentage point to 3.4%

key_facts.fact: IMF presented three scenarios: reference (3.1% growth, oil at $82/bbl), adverse (2.5%, oil at $100), and severe (2.0%, oil at $110+) — the severe scenario would be 'a close call for a global recession'
key_facts.excerpt: the IMF presented three growth scenarios: weaker, worse and severe... the severe scenario assumes an extended and deepening conflict... slashing global growth to 2.0%. 'This would mean a close call for a global recession'

key_facts.fact: Global inflation forecast raised to 4.4% for 2026, up from 4.1% in 2025 and the 3.8% the IMF had previously expected; in the severe scenario, inflation could exceed 6%
key_facts.excerpt: the IMF marked up its expectation for global inflation this year to 4.4% from 4.1% in 2025 and from the 3.8% it had forecast for this year in January

key_facts.fact: UK suffered the sharpest growth downgrade in the G7, with its forecast cut to 0.8% from 1.3%; US growth lowered slightly to 2.3%; eurozone to 1.1%
key_facts.excerpt: the UK would suffer the sharpest growth downgrade and joint highest inflation rate in the G7 this year... cut its forecast by 0.5 percentage points to 0.8%

key_facts.fact: IMF chief economist Gourinchas said the Iran war is a 'far bigger risk to the global economy than President Trump's initial wave of steep tariffs'
key_facts.excerpt: the war has created a far bigger risk to the global economy than President Donald Trump's initial wave of steep tariffs did a year ago, IMF chief economist Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas told Reuters

key_facts.fact: IMF cut Middle East and North Africa growth forecast to 1.1%, down from 3.9%; Iran's economy forecast to shrink 6.1% this year
key_facts.excerpt: It estimates that Iran's economy will shrink by 6.1% this year

stories.headline: ASML Beats Q1 Estimates With €8.8B Revenue, Raises 2026 Guidance to €36-40B on AI Demand

key_facts.fact: ASML Q1 net sales of €8.8B beat the €8.5B estimate; net profit of €2.8B beat the €2.5B estimate; gross margin of 53.0% at the high end of guidance
key_facts.excerpt: Net sales: 8.8 billion euros ($10.4 billion) versus 8.5 billion euros expected. Net profit: 2.8 billion euros versus 2.5 billion euros expected

key_facts.fact: ASML raised full-year 2026 net sales guidance to €36-40B from the previous €34-39B, with 51-53% gross margin
key_facts.excerpt: we now expect total net sales for 2026 to be between €36 billion and €40 billion, with a gross margin between 51% and 53%

key_facts.fact: CEO Fouquet: 'Demand for chips is outpacing supply. Our customers are accelerating their capacity expansion plans for 2026 and beyond'
key_facts.excerpt: The semiconductor industry's growth outlook continues to solidify, driven by ongoing AI-related infrastructure investments. Demand for chips is outpacing supply.

key_facts.fact: ASML can ship 60 flagship low-NA EUV tools in 2026 (25% more than 2025) and has capacity for 80 in 2027; each tool costs ~$300M
key_facts.excerpt: ASML should be able to ship 60 of its flagship low-NA EUV tools in 2026 - 25 per cent more than in 2025 - and will have capacity to ship 80 in 2027

key_facts.fact: 51% of net sales of new tools in Q1 went toward memory chips, up from 30% in Q4, reflecting the ongoing memory chip shortage
key_facts.excerpt: ASML said 51% of net sales of its new tools in the first quarter went toward memory, versus 30% in the previous quarter

key_facts.fact: This was the first quarter ASML stopped disclosing order numbers, a closely watched metric; Fouquet said intake 'continues to be very strong'
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first quarter where ASML has not disclosed order numbes which is typically a closely-watched metric by investors. Fouquet said Wednesday that ASML's order intake 'continues to be very strong'

stories.headline: Snap Plans to Lay Off 15-20% of Workforce as $400M Perplexity AI Deal Collapses

key_facts.fact: Snap is preparing to lay off 15-20% of its workforce of 5,261 employees, with some teams reduced by half; the layoffs could be announced as soon as Wednesday
key_facts.excerpt: layoffs could affect around 15-20% of Snap's workforce, which currently exceeds 5,000 employees. Some teams could even be reduced by half

key_facts.fact: CEO Evan Spiegel's memo says the company plans to cut costs and achieve profitability; there is uncertainty over how strongly the cuts will be framed as AI-driven
key_facts.excerpt: The newsletter also noted uncertainty over how strongly CEO Evan Spiegel will present these cuts as being driven by artificial intelligence

key_facts.fact: Snap's $400M integration deal with Perplexity AI, which would have embedded its AI answer engine within Snapchat, has fallen through due to disagreements over terms
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement would have seen Perplexity pay $400 million in cash and equity to embed its AI answer engine within Snapchat... the rollout was delayed due to disagreements over terms

key_facts.fact: The Specs AR glasses subsidiary is expanding hiring even as the legacy Snapchat business faces deep cuts; Snap has invested $3B+ over 11 years in AR glasses
key_facts.excerpt: the Specs organisation, recently spun off as a separate subsidiary, is hiring employees... The company has invested more than $3 billion over 11 years into developing its AR glasses

key_facts.fact: Activist investor Irenic Capital disclosed a 2.5% stake weeks ago and urged Snap to use AI to cut ~21% of workers and spin off or shut down Specs
key_facts.excerpt: Irenic said Snap should use AI more heavily to cut about 21% of its workforce, or 1,000 workers. 'AI can and should replace many existing roles,' Irenic said in its letter

stories.headline: Disney Lays Off ~1,000 Employees in New CEO D'Amaro's First Major Restructuring

key_facts.fact: Disney is eliminating ~1,000 roles, primarily from its newly consolidated enterprise marketing division under Chief Brand Officer Asad Ayaz; cuts also span studios, TV, ESPN, product & technology
key_facts.excerpt: The media company is eliminating about 1,000 roles, primarily as a result of Disney's formation of a consolidated enterprise marketing division under the leadership of Asad Ayaz

key_facts.fact: This is the first major restructuring action under CEO Josh D'Amaro, who succeeded Bob Iger on March 18; Disney had ~231,000 employees as of September 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Disney reported having about 231,000 full- and part-time employees as of September 2025. It's the first big restructuring action under D'Amaro, who took over as Disney's CEO on March 18 from Bob Iger

key_facts.fact: Marvel Studios was hit hard, losing nearly its entire visual development team — artists, character designers, environment designers — many with 10+ years at the company
key_facts.excerpt: Marvel has been hit hard as it is losing staff from both New York and Burbank... This comprises nearly the entire Academy Award-winning visual development team at Marvel Studios

key_facts.fact: Disney has already cut over 8,000 jobs since 2022; D'Amaro cited the need for 'a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce' in his employee memo
key_facts.excerpt: this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs

key_facts.fact: Disney is also merging staff across Disney+ and Hulu as the two streaming services complete their transition into a single integrated platform
key_facts.excerpt: Disney is also merging staff across Disney+ and Hulu as the two services complete their transition into a single integrated streaming experience

stories.headline: Maine Passes First US Statewide Data Center Moratorium, Blocking Facilities Over 20 MW

key_facts.fact: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium on new data centers exceeding 20 MW capacity until November 2027; House voted 79-62 and Senate 21-13, largely along party lines
key_facts.excerpt: The state's House passed it 79-62, and the Senate passed it 21-13—along party lines with a few exceptions

key_facts.fact: The 20 MW threshold is well below the average contemporary data center (~40 MW), effectively blocking construction of any AI-scale facility
key_facts.excerpt: the threshold is 20 megawatts, which is actually pretty low, and effectively blocks construction of what is commonly known as an AI data center. The average contemporary data center uses about 40 megawatts

key_facts.fact: Governor Janet Mills has signaled she may sign the bill but wants an exemption for a $550M project at a former paper mill in Jay that would bring much-needed local jobs
key_facts.excerpt: Governor Janet Mills has said the measure needs to have an exemption for a proposed $550 million project at the former Androscoggin paper mill in Jay to get her support

key_facts.fact: The bill creates a coordinating council of government officials and experts to evaluate the cost and impact of data centers on the state
key_facts.excerpt: the bill would pause approvals for data centers requiring more than 20 megawatts of power until late 2027, while a state council studies their impact on electricity grids, costs, and the environment

key_facts.fact: Similar legislative efforts are being discussed in 11 other US states; a Quinnipiac poll found 65% of Americans oppose having a data center built in their community
key_facts.excerpt: Similar proposals are currently being discussed by 11 other US states... A recent poll found 65% of Americans oppose having a data center built in their community

key_facts.fact: Maine ranks 4th highest in US electricity prices; lawmakers Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez introduced federal legislation last month to halt all data center construction until AI safety laws are passed
key_facts.excerpt: lawmakers Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced a legislation to halt all construction on data centers until Congress passes AI safety legislation

stories.headline: Global Smartphone Shipments Fall 4.1% YoY in Q1 2026, First Decline Since 2023

key_facts.fact: Worldwide smartphone shipments fell 4.1% year-over-year in Q1 2026, the first quarterly decline since 2023, driven by a memory chip supply crunch and record-high memory prices
key_facts.excerpt: Limited memory supply and record high memory prices increase pressure on smartphone OEMs to reduce shipments and increase prices that dampen demand

key_facts.fact: Samsung led global shipments, growing 3.6% YoY; Apple grew 3.3% YoY; all other major vendors saw year-over-year declines
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung led, followed by Apple, while other vendors fell YoY

key_facts.fact: The decline is linked to the memory chip shortage that has also driven demand for ASML equipment, as data center and AI workloads compete for limited chip supply
key_facts.excerpt: Limited memory supply and record high memory prices increase pressure on smartphone OEMs to reduce shipments and increase prices

key_facts.fact: Emerging markets face particular challenges ahead as the memory crunch and Iran war-driven cost pressures compound
key_facts.excerpt: Emerging markets will be a challenge in the year ahead

sources.title: Worldwide Smartphone Shipments Decline 4.1% in Q1 2026
